subject.title: Feature: unified provider fallback chains for all provider-backed tools (web_search, image/music/video generation, web_fetch)

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a shared core fallback-policy/configuration contract for provider-backed tools, or keep fallback behavior owner-specific and begin with the narrower web-search request?
rationale: The request adds configuration and failure-policy semantics across multiple tool families, and the supplied related reports show that failure classification and timeout behavior are still independently under discussion.

options.title: Design the shared contract first
options.body: Define supported failure classes, per-attempt deadlines, error aggregation, ownership boundaries, and backward-compatible configuration before accepting implementation work across tool families.

options.title: Scope the first increment to web search
options.body: Track the media and fetch extensions separately while resolving the concrete `web_search` fallback behavior in the existing narrower proposal.

options.title: Keep policies tool-specific
options.body: Reject a uniform config contract and allow each tool owner to expose retry or fallback only where its provider semantics justify it.

recommendation.title: Design the shared contract first
recommendation.body: Define supported failure classes, per-attempt deadlines, error aggregation, ownership boundaries, and backward-compatible configuration before accepting implementation work across tool families.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related open proposal directly covers the failure-class policy that a shared fallback contract would need to resolve.
